title: Why it exists
summary: Why an advisory firm runs a Lab, said once and large: a 96px claim (its day job is making the installs sharper) and one plain sentence under it, who pays for it (the advisory work).
story: The tease's second beat: before it is a product, the Lab is the R&D behind the installs (Q4), and the advisory work pays for it (Q4).
copy: [N, Q4] claim “The Lab’s day job is making our installs sharper.” (its day job now; the platform is its ambition)
[K, Q4] lede “Our advisory work pays for the Lab.”
phone: ≤1023: the claim takes the full measure (kit 64px), the lede under it. ≤767: the claim at the kit's 44px, the lede at 16px.

reference.borrowed: One statement carries the section; the one supporting line is short and sits quietly under it.
reference.kelwin: Kit §12.6 claim head (.ac-shead--claim, .ac-claim--xl, .ac-shead__lede), nothing of the page's own.

motion: entrance: the kit's: the seam draws, the label fades, the claim rises, the lede follows.
notes: Coherence pass 2: the claim steps down from 96 to 72px so the 120px h1 leads the page. Round 8's three-paragraph essay ('A CRM records what happened…', 'five tools with no shared memory', 'a generic model…') and its conclusion line are cut: they argued for instruments the founder now says not to name (Q4). Round 9's first build hung two keyed facts under the claim ('Paid for by', 'Your data'); they read as the old facts box moved down a section, so the funding is now one sentence and the data line is cut (Privacy carries it, with its draft status).
